name: Whitney Dankworth
title: Data Science • Causal Inference • Applied ML Engineering
welcome:
Welcome! I'm Whitney Dankworth — a Data Scientist at Microsoft working in causal inference and applied ML engineering, building systems that shape decisions and targeted messaging for billions of Windows users.

This portfolio is an interactive terminal.

Type 'help' to see available commands.

bio.summary: Statistics, computer science, and business — three lenses that let me frame problems and tell valuable stories. At Microsoft I work on causal inference, applied ML, and the infrastructure that lets a small team move decisions for billions of users. I value technical excellence and clear communication, from engineers to executives.
education: B.S. Business and Political Economy + B.A. Computer Science — New York University (Stern + CAS); Mathematics minor

highlights: Built tensor engineering infrastructure powering an ML retention model — featurizing 30 time-dependent signals across 700M Windows devices in an afternoon. ~1000% velocity improvement (weeks → days) and shipped the first model version to production for targeted device messaging. Mentored a PhD intern to train the first Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) in the Windows organization.
Designed a novel system for repeatable, interpretable causal analysis — scaling insights across hundreds of analysis variations without losing the interpretability needed to act on them.
Forecast Windows monthly active devices and Windows 10/11 mix for executive decision scenarios and fiscal-year target setting across hundreds of downstream metrics.

Modeled Windows in-device campaign "noise" and its effect on retention, quantifying the short-term-revenue vs long-term-product-health trade-off. Drove ongoing investment in "right message, right time" tooling. Windows Data "AI Enablement Champion."

Bootstrapped the standardized publishing layer for Windows device data across Microsoft (DataOps + cross-functional PM and engineering). 75% reduction in critical metric pipeline delays, hundreds of millions in revenue powered, and — as of 2026 — the most-used Windows device data source at Microsoft, feeding metrics reported weekly to senior leaders and in public earnings calls.
Modeled expected post-update device health for the Windows 11 rollout (ensemble ML + pattern mining); delivered bi-weekly model-interpretation reviews to the head of Windows during launch.
Modeled Windows lifetime value for executive decision scenarios around Windows 10 end of support.
Formulated methodology and delivered a POC for first-in-class ML modeling of Azure infrastructure health
COSINE (Core OS & Intelligent Edge) Data Science Team, Azure deployments
Built and maintained data pipelines to automate routine dashboarding
Manipulated 100MM+ rows of data using SQL for user taxonomy project
Classified 900+ advertisements for CTR, CPM, and revenue optimization
Used data analysis to assist advisors in rebalancing $50MM of discretionary client assets
Conducted investment research and advised financial advisors

projects.title: Raspberry Pi Email Summary Agent with Local Processing
projects.description: OpenClaw was an enticing offering, but security and privacy concerns prompted me to explore a local-first approach. I built a Raspberry Pi-based email summary agent that processes data locally and sends me a prioritized digest a few times per day. This project allowed me to experiment with local AI agent capabilities and edge computing while ensuring my data remains private and secure.
projects.status: Public — try it out with the code on my GitHub!

projects.title: wheresmybus — Real-Time Transit from the Terminal
projects.description: I kept missing my bus home from work because I was too deep in AI CLI tools like Claude Code and Copilot CLI. Ironically, I used one to fix the problem. wheresmybus is a Go CLI that gives me real-time King County Metro arrivals without ever leaving the terminal. It auto-detects whether I'm at home or the office via WiFi and shows the right stop — so now I just type `wheresmybus` and never miss the bus again.

projects.title: Agentic Workflows for Time-Series Feature Engineering
projects.description: Agentic workflows that assist data scientists with time-series feature engineering at scale — featurizing dozens of signals across hundreds of millions of devices in an afternoon, collapsing model-iteration cycles from weeks to days.

projects.title: Windows Device Semantic Data Model + AI Agents
projects.description: Led ideation and execution of a next-generation semantic data model for Windows device data at Microsoft, modernizing decade-old infrastructure. Powers RAG agents over primary Windows data assets and is now the most-used Windows device data source at the company.

projects.title: ICU Post-Discharge Mortality Prediction
projects.description: Predicting long-term mortality for ICU patients after discharge — classical ML + statistical modeling on clinical time-series data. NYU coursework in Data Science for Healthcare.

projects.title: News Topic Modeling + Bias Classification at Scale
projects.description: Topic-modeled and classified political bias across a large news corpus. Distributed Hadoop + PySpark pipeline for ingestion and feature extraction, LSTM classifier for bias prediction.
